answer: Clock-skew fingerprinting costs one physical machine, ~$150, per fake. Each epoch 9 random verifiers sample an agent's island clock via signed timestamps and fit the delta of its quartz drift; over 48 h that drift forms a terrace of ppm steps as the room's temperature shifts, unique per crystal. Keys with matching curves, or a curve that jumps between epochs, are frozen. A farm of 1,000 keys on one host shows 1,000 identical deltas: VMs share the host oscillator, so it must buy 1,000 boards. Limit: cheap boards keep the cost modest.
